penalties_applied.name: requires_human_fulfillment
penalties_applied.reason: Compliant travel booking requires real-time negotiation with airline systems, policy enforcement across GDS/NDC APIs, and ongoing exception handling — substantial per-booking human or deeply integrated automation work.

penalties_applied.name: requires_synchronous_human
penalties_applied.reason: Corporate travel programs typically involve approval workflows, exception escalations, and traveler support interactions that require synchronous human involvement.

rationale: The buyer — corporate travel managers at mid-to-large companies — is real, identifiable, and has budget; companies already pay for managed travel programs (Concur, TravelPerk, Egencia). However, the solution space requires deep GDS/NDC API integrations, airline policy compliance layers, and legal agreements that are entirely outside what a Claude prompt plus a landing page can deliver; buildability scores 3. More critically, operational autonomy is 2 — every booking exception, cancellation, and policy conflict requires human judgment, making this a consulting/agency play, not an autonomous micro-service. Total after penalties drops to 2.4.
solution_plan: Not recommended for build. The core problem — airlines actively blocking AI agents from their booking flows — requires either direct GDS partnerships or screen-scraping workarounds that violate airline ToS, neither of which a solo non-technical operator can build or maintain. This is a venture-scale infrastructure play (think a startup with airline commercial agreements), not a Claude-factory micro-service. A solo operator cannot realistically build, sell, or maintain this.
notes: Fails build gates: operational_autonomy=2 (min 7), buildability_with_ai=3 (min 6). Total 2.4 is below drop threshold.
